mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-01.title: Prime factorize
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-01.body:
J = 10, U = 21, L = 12, Y = 25. Product $= 10 \cdot 21 \cdot 12 \cdot 25 = (2 \cdot 5)(3 \cdot 7)(2^2 \cdot 3)(5^2) = 2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3 \cdot 7$.
$\sqrt{2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3 \cdot 7} = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5\sqrt{2 \cdot 5 \cdot 7} = 30\sqrt{70}$, so $b = 70$.

**Answer: 70**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-01.title: Compute the product
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-01.body:
$10 \cdot 21 \cdot 12 \cdot 25 = 63{,}000 = 900 \times 70$, and $\sqrt{900} = 30$. 70 = $2 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$ has no square factor, so $\sqrt{63000} = 30\sqrt{70}$ and $b = 70$.

**Answer: 70**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-02.title: Use the prime factorization
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-02.body:
JULY's word-product is $2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3 \cdot 7$. N = 14 $= 2 \cdot 7$, leaving $2^2 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^3$.
Three factors of 5 must come from different letters whose values are multiples of 5, other than J (10) and Y (25): only E = 5, O = 15 and T = 20. Together they give $5 \cdot 15 \cdot 20 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5^3$, leaving a factor $3$: C = 3.
Letters C, E, N, O, T in alphabetical order: **CENOT**. (Adding A = 1 would not change the product; ACENOT is also accepted.)

**Answer: CENOT**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-02.title: Check the product
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-02.body:
$C \cdot E \cdot N \cdot O \cdot T = 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 14 \cdot 15 \cdot 20 = 63{,}000$ and $J \cdot U \cdot L \cdot Y = 10 \cdot 21 \cdot 12 \cdot 25 = 63{,}000$ ✓. No letters repeat or come from JULY.

**Answer: CENOT**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-03.title: Center at the average
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-03.body:
JULY's word-sum is $10 + 21 + 12 + 25 = 68$, average 17. A four-term arithmetic sequence is symmetric about its average: $17 - \frac{3d}{2}, 17 - \frac{d}{2}, 17 + \frac{d}{2}, 17 + \frac{3d}{2}$. For whole numbers $d$ must be even: $d = 2$: 14, 16, 18, 20; $d = 4$: 11, 15, 19, 23; $d = 6$: 8, 14, 20, 26; $d = 8$ would need 29 > 26. Least value: **8**.

**Answer: 8**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-03.title: Equation
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-13-03.body:
$a + (a + d) + (a + 2d) + (a + 3d) = 4a + 6d = 68$, so $2a + 3d = 34$. To make $a$ small, make $d$ large, but $a + 3d \le 26$. $d = 6$: $a = 8$, largest term $26$ ✓; $d = 8$: $a = 5$, largest $29$ ✗. So the least value is 8.

**Answer: 8**
